about: The Memorare is a Marian prayer of supplication. It recalls the confidence that no one who sought Mary's protection, implored her help, and asked her intercession was abandoned. Inspired by that confidence, the sinner stands before the Mother of the Word and asks her graciously to hear and heed the speaker's words.

s01.translation: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that it has never been heard

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s02.translation: that anyone who runs to your protection, implores your help, and seeks your intercession was abandoned.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s03.translation: Inspired by this confidence, I run to you, O Virgin of virgins and Mother;

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s04.translation: I come to you; before you I stand, a grieving sinner.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s05.translation: O Mother of the Word, do not despise my words,

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s06.translation: but hear them graciously and heed them.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

w001.function: Formally the singular passive imperative of “mémoro”, used with the sense “be mindful, remember”.

w005.function: A vocative name in apposition to “Virgo”.

w007.function: With “audítum”, forms a perfect passive infinitive in the report governed by “Memoráre”.

w008.function: A neuter participle in the impersonal “esse audítum”: “it has been heard”. It modifies no expressed nominal.

w010.function: An ablative after “a” with temporal force: from ages past, ever.

w011.function: The accusative subject of “esse derelíctum” in indirect statement.

w014.function: The first of three parallel participles modifying “quemquam”.

w022.function: With “derelíctum”, forms a perfect passive infinitive whose accusative subject is “quemquam”.

w026.function: A passive participle referring to the speaker “Ego” and giving the motive for the following verbs.

w027.function: An ablative with “animátus”: the confidence by which the speaker is inspired.

w031.function: A genitive dependent on the title “Virgo”: Virgin of virgins.

w040.function: A predicative apposition to the speaker. “Gemens” describes the same sinner.

w042.function: Together with “despícere”, forms a negative command.

w044.function: A genitive dependent on “Mater”, referring to the divine Word.

w047.function: An infinitive complementing “Noli”, with “verba mea” as its object.

w050.function: A predicate adjective referring to the understood feminine subject of “audi”.

w052.function: The second imperative intensifies the request after simple “audi”. The speaker's words remain the understood object.
